note: The noun’s consonants supply the root key. Its derivation from a Hebrew verb תהה is uncertain.
summary: Genesis calls the earth תֹּהוּ while darkness covers the deep. Isaiah sets this condition against the earth being inhabited.

senses.definition: An uninhabited waste, said of the earth or of a tract of land.

evidence.note: The earth is called תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ while darkness covers the deep.
The denial that God created the earth תֹהוּ is followed by the purpose for which he formed it, לָשֶׁבֶת, to be inhabited.
Leaders wander through a תֹּהוּ where there is no path.
